title: Controllers: the pad in use, controller choice and sensitivity
summary: Gameplay now follows the controller you are actually using, not the first one the browser lists. Chrome on Windows often lists idle virtual pads first (Steam Input, DS4Windows), which left a real controller doing nothing while riding. A new Controller Settings page (Settings → Controls, from the main menu or Pause) chooses Auto or a specific connected controller and tunes steering, lean, gas/brake and camera sensitivity plus the stick dead zone.
details: Fix shipped in PR #160 (live); Controller Settings in PR #161.
Named after the original Options → Controller Settings page. The original ControllerSelect page let four split-screen players press × to claim a pad; Auto plays that role for one rider.
Sensitivity is a port enhancement (the original has none): 100% keeps the current response and full stick travel always reaches full lock; the 15% default dead zone is unchanged.
Menus follow the same controller, so idle devices cannot navigate them.
Verified: Rust menu tests, unit tests, and test_settings, test_pause_menu, test_bindings, test_frontend browser tests; a regression test lists an idle virtual pad first.
limitation: Not tested on a physical Windows machine or real controller. Host captures; Controller Settings is not yet a verified public release.
